newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - July 29.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
GUJRAL, VAJPAYEE CLASH OVER OFFER TO MILITANTS

Prime Minister Gujral told the lower house of parliament that there was no compromise on the stand that the entire Jammu and Kashmir as it existed before 1947 was part of India. Leader of the Opposition Atal Behari Vajpayee repeatedly sought to draw attention to reports that the prime minister was willing to hold unconditional talks with the militants provided they laid down their arms. Gujral replied that there was a distinction between militants from across the border with whom the government was not prepared to talk at all and the "misguided youth" on the Indian side of the border.
Indian Express
CONGRESS SUPPORTS RABRI DEVI IN CONFIDENCE VOTE

Bihar state Chief Minister Rabri Devi won the confidence vote with the support of 136 members as compared to 110 who opposed her in the 324 member state assembly. Supporting the confidence motion, Congress party leader Ramashray Prasad Singh said his party's decision to support the Rabri ministry was taken following the resignation of Laloo Yadav. The Congress, he said, had already made it clear that it will have no objection in voting for the Rahstriya Janata Dal party with a new leader.
The Economic Times
INDIA PROMISES TO SLASH TARIFFS

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told the Association of South East Asian Nations' post-ministerial conference that India would lower tariffs to the Asian level by the year 2000 and to world levels a little later. He also reiterated India's commitment to going convertible on the capital account in a phased manner.
SIEMENS POSTPONES $500 MLN INVESTMENT IN INDIA

The Siemens AG has deferred its proposed $500 million investment plan in India till the economic situation in the country improves. It has already invested $500 million in India and had promised to invest another $500 million before the turn of the century. A sudden slow down in the Indian economy and huge losses in its Indian operations forced the German giant to postpone the new investments. Dr Heinrich V Pierer who is president and chief executive officer of Siemens AG said the problem with India was its bureaucracy.
Financial Express
WORLD BANK WARNS THERMAL POWER CORPORATION

The World Bank warned the National Thermal Power Corporation (NTPC) it will suspend the ongoing loans and defer future ones if it (NTPC) failed to recover the 50 billion rupee dues from the state electricity boards. The NTPC has received loans worth about $4 billion from the World Bank since 1975. Suspension of the loans will seriously affect the completion of many major projects which are being funded or are being appraised for loans by the Bank. NTPC officials said they had already begun actions and power was being supplied strictly against advance payments or against irrevocable letters of credit.
INDIA TRYING FOR BERTH IN ASIA PACIFIC ECONOMIC COOPERATION

India made a strong pitch for a birth in the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) criteria with its strong economic growth and irreversible reforms. Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told the post ministerial conference of the ASEAN meet in Kuala Lumpur that India would soon meet the criteria of comparability with other APEC members. He pointed out that India now had foreign exchange reserves of $29 billion and foreign investments worth $6.5 billion and an average seven percent gross domestic product growth rate for the last three years.
Business Standard
GLOBAL GIANTS TO INVEST 11.39 BLN IN INDIA

Five multinational companies from the United States and the United Kingdom have come together to form a consortium to invest 11.39 billion rupees as equity in India in 100 percent export oriented petro products units. The consortium will have 49.06 percent equity stake in the units. The remaining 50.94 percent will be held by Indian shareholders. The Indian consortium PRA Petrochemicals has projected an export turnover of 336.07 rupees in five years. The project is expected to be set up in two years and will begin feeding the international market soon after.
EUROPEAN UNION PLANS BAN ON INDIAN SEAFOOD

The European Union (EU) is planning to ban import of seafood from India saying they are unhygienic. If imposed, the ban will cost India 15 billion rupees a year. The Commerce Ministry fears that the European Union's move may affect India's seafood exports worth 35 billion rupees a year to Japan and the United States. The EU has already suspended imports from four Indian seafood companies. The Union has threatened a total ban on Indian seafood after a team sent by it visited Indian seafood companies. The team did not find the seafood production environment very hygienic. It said unless the hygiene met EU standards it could not allow import of seafood from India.
BOURSE REGULATOR PLANS NEW REGIME FOR FRESH ISSUES

The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) plans to eliminate the role of banks in hawking new issues, cut issue costs and do away with the refunding of issue proceeds in case an issue fails. It also plans to drastically cut the time for the completion of an issue. The scheme will also complement the book-building process of selling an issue. The proposed changes are based on the recommendations of the Dave Committee.
